Peter Kropotkin, Mutual Aid.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/peter-kropotkin/mutual-aid

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Peter Kropotkin, the annotator and the author and the writer of an introduction, died 1921 (Wikidata Q5752, P570 = 1921-02-08; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Kropotkin).

First publication of the text used: 'Mutual Aid was published in 1902 by Peter Kropotkin. Weijia Cheng sponsored the production of this ebook for Standard Ebooks. It was produced by Alex Cabal, and is based on a transcription produced in 2003 by Charles Aldarondo for Project Gutenberg and on digital scans from Google Books. The cover page is adapted from Flock of Geese, a painting completed in 1883 by Elizabeth Nourse. The cover and title pages feature the League Spartan and Sorts Mill Goudy typefaces created in 2014 and 2009 by The League of Moveable Type. The first edition of this ebook was released on August 27, 2021, 11:57 p.m. You can check for updates to this ebook, view its revision history, or download it for different ereading systems at standardebooks.org/ebooks/peter-kropotkin/mutual-aid. The volunteer-driven Standard Ebooks project relies on readers like you to submit typos, corrections, and other improvements. Anyone can contribute at standardebooks.org..' (SE colophon).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1902, before 1929. Works published before 1929 entered the United States public domain by 1 January 2025, and Standard Ebooks states the same in its rights statement (below).
- Country of origin: every person whose words are in the text died in 1921 or earlier; the last to die was Peter Kropotkin in 1921 (Wikidata Q5752, P570 = 1921-02-08). So the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever its country of first publication.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
